title: Component Convergence and Interaction Heuristics for Compact Dashboard Rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: create a converged set of compact, reusable components and a small interaction heuristics guide to be used by the Console dashboard rollouts team. The outcome should allow product teams to assemble dense cost and rollout views with predictable spacing, token usage, and accessible interaction states. This ticket covers token mapping, a compact component kit (cards, micro-rail, status pills, compact tables), and a short heuristic doc for trade-offs (density vs discoverability).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Figma component library contains compact variants for cards, metric chips, status pills, micro-rail, and compact table row with tokens mapped to console theme variables.
A2: Interaction heuristics doc (1 page) explains when to choose compact vs standard variants and lists accessibility contrast/hit-area rules.
A3: Dev handoff artifact (token mapping JSON + usage examples) uploaded and linked; engineers confirm compatibility with runtime-1.18 token names.
A4: PM sign-off on visual density trade-offs and rollout checklist completed.
A5: Two sample dashboard routes implemented as prototypes demonstrating fallbacks for long labels and responsiveness to small widths.
A6: Performance note: tokens and components do not introduce additional expensive reflows in Console (baseline validated by ENG-1842).
design_notes: We aim to reduce the number of bespoke compact components by converging on variant-driven primitives. Key token considerations: spacing scale compresses by one step for compact palette; elevation is flattened to two discrete states; focus and hover should preserve 44px readable targets by expanding interactive hitboxes while keeping visual density compact. Use color tokens (semantic) rather than raw color to allow automatic contrast adjustments. Prototyping focused first on the Cost Explorer and Rollout Inspector since they require highest density. Consider accessibility: at compact sizes, use bold micro-typography + increased contrast for primary numbers. Add micro-animation only on expand/collapse to avoid motion noise.
decisions: D1: Use existing 'card' primitive as base; implement a 'compact' variant instead of creating a separate compact-card component.
D2: Spacing token map: compact uses --space-1 for internal paddings where standard uses --space-2; outer margins remain standard to preserve layout rhythm.
D3: Status pills will use semantic token names (status-success, status-warning, status-error) and a thin outline at compact sizes to maintain legibility.
D4: For metric typography, choose Demi (600) for primary metrics at 14px rather than increasing font-size; improves perceived weight without shifting layout.
D5: Motion minimized: only use 'expand' transition for cards; disable ephemeral hover transitions to reduce render churn.
D6: Accessibility: maintain 3:1 contrast for secondary text and 4.5:1 for primary numbers in compact mode where possible; document exceptions for badge overprints.
D7: Implementation will map token names to runtime-1.18 compatible variables; engineering to validate token substitution in Dedicated and Private builds.
open_questions: Q1: Should compact table rows collapse secondary columns into a tooltip on very narrow widths, or should we support horizontal scroll? Need PM preference for discoverability vs content permanence.
Q2: Do we allow denser grid (reduce gutters globally) for specific routes behind a rollout flag, or prefer per-component compact variants only?
Q3: What telemetry event should indicate a user has switched from standard to compact density (if we add a toggle)? Product to advise.
Q4: Engineering: will existing token pipeline support dynamic theme overrides for compact variants without a build? (ENG confirmation required)
Q5: Localization: do compact labels need special truncation rules for languages with longer words? i18n team to advise.
